why: srand: the seed of every random draw; must be ported (Darklands.Core.Randomness / the srand call sites cite it)
rand: the MSC 6 generator (holdrand*214013+2531011) feeds every roll; ported as MscRandom (Oracle:core.json)
time(0): reseeds the generator (srand(time(0))); ported as GameState.ClockSeed with a DIVERGENCE note at each call site
__aFldiv: signed 32-bit division of C long; the C# divides long/int with `// C:` notes where width or sign matters (TRACEABILITY rule 3)
__aFlmul: 32-bit multiplication of C long; C# long/int arithmetic at the call site
__aFlrem: signed 32-bit remainder of C long; C# % at the call site
__aFNaldiv: long /= long in place; C# arithmetic at the call site
__chkstk: stack probe the compiler inserts in big frames; no effect on the game

Microsoft C 6.0 run-time library (crt0 + LIBC: start-up, stdio, strings, DOS calls, printf engine, heap). Replaced by .NET: file access by Darklands.Content/Persistence, strings and number formatting by the BCL; the call sites cite the C call (strcpy, sprintf, fopen ...) where its semantics matter. rand/srand/time are listed above as game logic
RTLink/Plus 16-byte stub segment; overlay loading has no counterpart in a flat .NET program
RTLink/Plus overlay manager (vector handler, section loader); every vector is resolved to its target by this audit, overlays are ordinary classes in the C#
RTLink/Plus overlay cache (EMS/XMS/disk); memory management of overlays, no game effect
EMS driver interface (int 67h: present/allocate/map/free pages); .NET memory replaces expanded memory
heap-take/heap-give-back: DOS memory blocks with the "Insufficient system memory" exit; .NET allocation
heap/swap-file manager core (XMS, EMS and swap-file block moves); the C# keeps its data in memory (no heap.fng, no swap)
heap/swap-file manager (spill-file-create/save/load of the work buffers, hash table); data stays in .NET memory
heap/swap-file manager start-up (heap.fng, TMP/TEMP, EMS/XMS detection); function-level matches in the reference, but no game logic: buffers stay in memory
twin of R026 1ef8 (XMS block moves) linked into the battlefield loader; see R026
twin of R026 1f09 (swap-file block I/O); see R026
twin of R026 1f1d (EMS block moves); see R026
twin of R027 1f48 (swap blocks and hash table); see R027
twin of R028 1f48 (swap start-up); see R028
route-ems-enable: maps the path-finder's EMS page; the C# path finder keeps its tables in memory
route-ems-disable: unmaps the path-finder's EMS page

graphics/timer/sound driver interface: the self-patched far-jump table into MGRAPHIC.EXE and the sound drivers, the int 8 timer, page and palette calls. Replaced by IHost (IVideo, IAudio, IClock); the drawing the game asks for is ported in Darklands.Presentation, the sound and music in Darklands.Audio, the timer in IClock
page-to-page-box-copy: copies a rectangle between video pages (save/restore under boxes); Presentation redraws instead (Screen/ScreenDrawing)
palette-keep: reads the VGA palette (DAC); Presentation keeps its palette in memory
palette-reload: writes the saved VGA palette back
VGA DAC palette writes (port 3C8h/3C9h) and screen blits used by the PAN player and palette fades; IVideo.Present with the palette replaces them
VGA screen copy/fill used by the PAN player; IVideo replaces it
palette-ramp's speed calibration (a timing loop that measures the machine); the C# fade runs on IClock time
palette-ramp's DAC read (inp/outp port 3C7h/3C9h); Presentation keeps the palette in memory
video-probe/video-reset: VGA detection and BIOS video mode on exit; the host opens its own window
text-cursor-position-call (int 10h); no text cursor in the host
BIOS video (int 10h) text output used by the start-up messages
installs the int 9 keyboard handler (044A:020E: arrow/keypad state in 880h..889h); IInput (Darklands.Platform) delivers keys, the game logic reads them through GameUi
removes the int 9 keyboard handler
dos-text-print: int 21h/09h text output of start-up and fatal messages; the host reports errors itself
int 21h query used by main's start-up checks (DOS version/memory); host start-up
int 21h call of game-exit (terminate); the host closes the program
helper of 044a_0100 (int 21h)
dos-memory-grab: int 21h/48h memory block; .NET allocation
dos-memory-release: int 21h/49h; .NET allocation
int 21h/4Ah resize memory block; .NET allocation
strupr of a near string (a-z to A-Z); C# ToUpperInvariant on the ASCII names at the call site
far strcpy (near to far); C# string assignment
strcpy far to near (used by the text drawing); C# string assignment
strlen of a far string; C# Length
memset of a far buffer; C# Array.Fill/new arrays
memcmp of far buffers (returns the remaining count); C# SequenceEqual at the call site

file I/O helpers: open/create/close/read/save whole files, catalogs (.CAT) and their directory, picture files drawn from disk (image-paint); Darklands.Content (GameFiles, catalog and PIC readers) and Darklands.Persistence read and write the same files
picture-file-* buffered file reader of the PAN player (open/read/eof/close); the C# PanDecoder reads the whole file
PAN ring buffer: makes room for the next read so the reader does not overtake the cel being shown; the C# reads the whole file first and shows the same cels at the same rate (Cinematics, PanDecoder)
PAN player's empty interrupt routine (iret) installed while streaming
PAN ring buffer: copies n bytes between linear addresses
PAN ring buffer: reads a word at a linear address
PAN ring buffer: reset of the read/show positions
game-exit: restores video, removes the handlers, frees memory and exits to DOS; the host closes the window (quit is ported in the menu bar and hot keys)
data-file-drop: closes the open catalogs before a reload; Darklands.Content opens files per read
main: start-up (config, memory, drivers, fonts) and the call of the main loop root 03A1; the hosts (Darklands.Host.*) and DarklandsGame do this, the main loop itself is ported
start-up memory check (EMS/XMS and the swap store, with the EMS error texts); no memory limits in .NET

the manual's symbol check (copy-protection-entry with its pictures and retries) only gates play; the C# skips the question (as the later CD release does) but makes its five random draws first (roll-below 4, 20, 7, 7, 6: CopyProtection.Draw), so the generator goes on as the original's; no other game state depends on it
memory-debug-tracker: the developers' memory statistics in a battle; no game effect
word-array-fill(ptr, value, n): fill n words of a near array; the battle code's callers (fight-main-loop, fighter-collision-pass, floor-view-paint, R019 0C80) clear their arrays with Array.Clear/Fill
word-array-fill-far: the same for a far array (fight-draw's tile tables, 1DB7:0028's trackers); Array.Fill in the C#
index of a byte in a far array or n (route-tracker-table: the end of a path, the first 0xFF step); the C# path finder keeps the length itself
word-position(far array, value, n): the first index holding the word, or n (nudge_pile, floor-view-paint, 14F7:118E: the screen tile of a cell); ITacticalView.ScreenTileOf
allocates the party members' animation buffers with their sizes from TACANIM.DB; the C# animation library holds the decoded files
level-read: points the combat buffers (sprite lists, trackers, loot list) into the battle's segments; .NET objects replace the layout
shields-read: loads the party's shield pictures (pics\shieldX.pic) for the loot screen and keeps the old handles; the C# party panel loads its pictures itself
shields-release: frees those pictures and puts the old handles back
